fields.corePath: A wedding planner in Jaipur uses ShaadiDesk to keep her vendors straight. Step 1, she opens the site and clicks Add a wedding, and types the couple's first names and the date. Step 2, she opens the vendor board for that wedding and adds vendors one by one — decorator, caterer, pandit, mehendi artist, photographer, band — with the quote each one gave and the advance she has paid. Step 3, each vendor card moves through Enquired, Quoted, Booked, Advance paid, Done. Step 4, seven days before the wedding the site shows her the vendors who are still not confirmed as a red list. Step 5, she taps Send reminders and gets one WhatsApp message per pending vendor, already written with the wedding date and what is pending from them. Step 6, after the wedding she taps Close wedding and it gives her a one-page summary of what was quoted against what was actually paid, which she uses when she quotes the next family.
fields.knownGaps: Two things are stubbed. The vendor directory — where a planner could search other planners' vendors by city and see who actually turned up — is not built at all, that is phase two and I have not written a line of it. And the reminders only go on WhatsApp, not SMS, which matters because about a third of the older decorators and pandits in Jaipur do not use WhatsApp and the planner still has to ring them. Everything on the board itself is solid. The advance amounts are rupees only with no paise. There is no way to attach the vendor's quotation PDF to the card yet, so she keeps that in Drive and the card just has the number. Closing a wedding is one-way, there is no reopening it if a payment comes in late, and that has already bitten one planner in my testing. The first load is slow, about three seconds, because I am loading two font families I do not really need. None of these are on the core path.

render.domText:
ShaadiDesk
Every vendor. Every wedding. One board.

Coming soon for wedding planners in Jaipur, Udaipur and Delhi NCR.

The big fat Indian wedding runs on forty WhatsApp groups.
If you are planning six weddings this season, you already know where this goes. The decorator says one number in March and another in November. The caterer's advance is in a chat you cannot find. The pandit confirms and then does not.

ShaadiDesk keeps every vendor, every quote and every advance for every wedding in one board you can open at the venue.

Be the first to try it

There is no app, no board, no login, and no link into a product.
